Search Problem The form of the search process model will start the search function on each change that occurs, that is, on each deletion or addition of a character. Problems with this run: - The number of many requests on the server, one request per change. - If the oldest request, and the response is retrieved after the last request, the data will be displayed based on the old request, not the new one. For example: the user typed the word (Burger), there will be 6 requests, which is the number of changes that occurred in the text, which is the addition of 6 letters. Assuming th

be 6 requests, which is the number of changes that occurred in the text, which is the addition of 6 letters. Assuming that the response was retrieved in 300ms, and at the sixth character completed in 200ms, the data retrieved from the last response made at the third character will be displayed. The Solution: with many attempts, we came up with a solution that solves the two problems, the large number of requests and the appearance of wrong data. After making each change to the search text, it will wait 200-300ms before sending the request, accordingly the following will happen: if another change is made before the time [38] expires, the time is renewed again and so on, otherwise the request will be sent, if the user changes the search text, any previous request is canceled and the time starts over and so on. Overview Students at Birzeit University face a number of challenges that affect their ability to fully engage in campus life. There is no single official or well-organized system that allows students to access student activities, follow announcements, communicate with student bodies, or exchange study resources in a reliable way. Instead, communication is scattered 7 across social media platforms and temporary messaging groups, which makes it difficult for students to stay informed and participate effectively. essaging groups, which makes it difficult for students to stay informed and participate effectively. On platforms such as Facebook and WhatsApp, students are often divided into multiple unofficial groups, and not all students are members of the same ones. As a result, important announcements about events, activities, or elections may not reach all students in time, or may not reach them at all. This lack of centralization leads to confusion, missed opportunities, and reduced student engagement in university life. In addition, students frequently receive information that is not relevant to their academic or student-related activities, which increases information overload and limits effective participation. These internal challenges are further affected by the wider political and digital environment in which Birzeit University operates. As a university located in Palestine, student life is

ical and digital environment in which Birzeit University operates. As a university located in Palestine, student life is influenced by restrictions on freedom of expression and digital surveillance. On public platforms, students may feel unsafe sharing opinions or organizing activities, as content may be monitored, removed, or reported. This atmosphere discourages open communication and limits student expression. Students also face difficulties in finding used books, study tools, or reliable updates related to student activities and elections. Without a unified and secure platform, they often depend on personal networks that may exclude new or less-connected students. These issues negatively affect both academic engagement and community building on campus. The following are the eight types of tests we conducted on the project: 63 - Unit Testing:  Purpose: To test individual units or components of the software application.  Method: Developers write tests for each function or module; these tests are run every time the code changes to ensure that no new errors have been introduced. - Integration Testing:  Purpose: To expose faults in the interaction between integrated units.  Method: Combining individual software modules and testing them as a group, often using techniques like top-down, bottom- up, and sandwich testing. - System Testing:  Purpose: To validate the software as a whole and ensure it meets the specified requirements.  Method: Conducted on a complete, integrated system to evaluate the system's compliance with it

specified requirements.  Method: Conducted on a complete, integrated system to evaluate the system's compliance with its specified requirements. - User Acceptance Testing (UAT):  Purpose: To determine if the system satisfies the business needs and requirements.  Method: Typically performed by the end-users to ensure the software can handle required tasks in real-world scenarios, often following real-world usage scenarios. - Performance Testing:  Purpose: To test the behaviour of the system under certain conditions.  Method: Involves load testing (determining how the system behaves under heavy loads) and stress testing (how the system behaves under extreme conditions). - Security Testing:  Purpose: To identify any weaknesses, vulnerabilities, or threats in the software.  Method: Includes tests like penetration testing, vulnerability scanning, and risk assessment. - Compatibility Te

ware.  Method: Includes tests like penetration testing, vulnerability scanning, and risk assessment. - Compatibility Testing:  Purpose: To check the compatibility of the software with different environments.  Method: Testing how the software operates in various environments, including different web browsers, database versions, hardware, operating systems, mobile devices, and network environments. 64 - Regression Testing:  Purpose: To ensure that recent code changes haven't adversely affected existing features.  Method: Re-running previously passed tests on new software versions to check that existing functionality remains unaffected by new development. 10. rases in unstructured text—such as individual names, locations, and organizations—and categorizing them into predefined groups. This capability is essential for various NLP tasks including machine translation, question answering, entity linking, and relation extraction. These identified words or phrases are known as named entities (NEs). 23 However, NER faces challenges when texts contain named entities that are nested or overlapping. These situations give rise to what is known as nested entities or entity nesting. Such complexities are prevalent in specific domain-oriented datasets. While most research has focused on resolving flat entities, the challenges posed by nested entities often remain unaddressed. Named Entity Recognition serves as a bridge between unstructured text and structured data, enabling machines to sift through vast amounts of textual information and extract valuable d

d text and structured data, enabling machines to sift through vast amounts of textual information and extract valuable data in categorized forms. By pinpointing specific entities within a sea of words, NER fundamentally transforms how we process and utilize textual data. The primary purpose of NER is to comb through unstructured text, identify specific chunks as named entities, and classify them into predefined categories. This conversion of raw text into structured information makes the data more actionable, facilitating tasks like data analysis, information retrieval, and knowledge graph construction. Due to the encoding, the amount of data needed to represent the path between the user’s location and the chosen pharmacy’s location is reduced. Firstly, the user’s latitude and longitude and the chosen pharmacy’s latitude and longitude are found a

tion is reduced. Firstly, the user’s latitude and longitude and the chosen pharmacy’s latitude and longitude are found and stored within an empty list. Each character in the encoded string is decoded by being converted into a number by subtracting 63 from its ASCII code. After each character is decoded, the numbers were combined (From the unique numbers of each character) using bitwise 17 operations until the original value is finally retrieved. The decoded number shows how much the latitude and longitude have changed from their previous point. uage processing (NLP). It is primarily designed for practical applications, enabling the development of systems capable of processing and comprehending substantial amounts of text data. line laws were enforced in an attempt to deal with this issue, and as a solution, websites and companies were obligated to cite what information they collect, and to do so, users have to consent to give in their info manually, this sounds good and all, but there’s a catch, the average user won't read a full 10 pages legal agreement that includes between the lines what info they’re collecting, plus what is done to that data, and due to that inconvenience, users end up agreeing to whatever is written there, with the hope that its “not that bad”. With Policy Peek, it's not up to hope anymore! users don’t need to worry about what private information they’re giving to websites; it's not a matter of reading now after installing the Policy Peek extension, all the work will be lifted on behalf of the user, and it will filter the privacy policy of each website users visit in real-time, then it wi

lifted on behalf of the user, and it will filter the privacy policy of each website users visit in real-time, then it will give a summarized version of all the data being collected in a user-friendly interface, with a colorful indicator rating the privacy level users are risking, to give them a much quicker clear idea of what they’re signing up to. t operates by identifying the 'k' closest data points (neighbors) to a given query point based on a chosen distance metric we pick cosine similarity. The object serves as a uniform interface to three different algorithms. Here, for our project, we used the brute-force algorithm. The K-NN algorithm assumes that a new case/data is similar to available cases and classifies a new case into the category it most similar. The K-NN algorithm stores all the available data and classifies a new data point based on the similarity. This means that having the new data appears then it can be easily classified in suitable category using the K-NN algorithm. In ad- dition, it is known as a lazy learner algorithm since it does not learn from the set of training at the current time; instead, it stores the dataset, and at the time of classification, it acts on the dataset. d, it stores the dataset, and at the time of classification, it acts on the dataset. The KNN algorithm just stores the dataset in the training phase, and when new data is received, it classifies that data into a category that is very similar to the latest data. What is the cosine similarity? Cosine similarity is a measure used to determine the similarity between two vectors in a high-dimensional space. In our recommenders system, cosine similarity is commonly applied to calculate the similarity between the preferences or characteristics of different food items or user profiles. Data Collection: We used the following datasets to build a data frame with 2 labels (crying , non-crying):  Donate-a-cry: the only available public dataset in the field of baby crying detection, it consists of a diverse set of crying sounds, around 457 recordings.  Silence and Noise Dataset: contains recordings of silence and white noise to help the model distinguish baby cries from common background noises.  Children Talking Dataset: consists of children talking normally recordings, to help the model to distinguish between crying and ot

alking Dataset: consists of children talking normally recordings, to help the model to distinguish between crying and other vocalizations. Feature Extraction: The process of transforming audio signals into numerical features suitable for machine learning analysis. 49 Features:  MFCC ( Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients): Captures the audio signals’ timbral texture, represents the spectral of the audio, it’s important for differentiating between sound types since it reflects the way in which humans hear. To make the feature simpler, we took the mean of the MFCC values.  Zero-Crossing Rate: Indicates how often the

s hear. Abstract A website that uses an Arabic Handwritten Recognition (AHR) offline system is proposed. This web site will use a web application as a front that takes images of handwritten Arabic text and sends them to an Intelligent Character Recognition (ICR) system. This system in turn will extract any Arabic words found, convert them to printed text, and return the converted text to the web application. The ICR system used for this app is an enhanced implementation of the Optical Character Recognition (OCR) technology, where ICR is used to recognize handwritten text and OCR is used for typewriting. The ICR system in AHR will use pre-processing techniques to remove excess noise in the image, segment

for typewriting. The ICR system in AHR will use pre-processing techniques to remove excess noise in the image, segment the words and perform any necessary action before recognizing the word. The ICR system will use Neural Networks, an algorithm used in deep learning, to distinguish and recognize characters and ligatures. By using this app, those who require a product to convert handwritten Arabic text to printed text can easily complete their task by using this website. The AHR system will rely on a Deep Convolutional Neural Network (DCNN) with a Bi- Directional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM) neural network and Connectionist Temporal Classification (CTC) loss to perform the recognition of the Arabic words. oduction 1.1Introduction Public transportation plays an essential role in our daily lives, particularly for workers and university students who rely on it to commute. However, the public transportation system in the West Bank faces several challenges that make commuting inefficient and inconvenient. One of the main issues is the absence of published departure schedules. Buses, vans, and cars depart only when they are full, leading to long and unpredictable wait times. Additionally, driver scheduling is managed manually through handwritten lists, often causing confusion and disputes over turn-order. Additionally, each official transportation line has only two main stops. This lack of intermediate stops forces many passengers to rely on expensive private transportation, such as yellow taxis. During our exchange program abroad, we observed how structured and efficient pub- lic transportatio

uch as yellow taxis. During our exchange program abroad, we observed how structured and efficient pub- lic transportation systems can be. Apps like Google Maps provide detailed travel information, including the best routes, estimated travel times, departure and arrival schedules, and total distances. Other applications even display ticket prices and suggest multiple route options based on real-time availability. These technologies op- timize public transport by offering convenient and data-driven solutions for passengers. Inspired by these systems, we decided to develop a mobile application that adapts these advanced technologies to fit the transportation system in the West Bank. Unlike traditional ride-hailing apps that simply assign the nearest driver, our algorithm matches based on arrival time synchronization to minimize waiting time for both parties. The matching process works as follows: 1.Calcul

arrival time synchronization to minimize waiting time for both parties. The matching process works as follows: 1.Calculate the passenger’s ETA to the pickup point based on walking distance and average walking speed. 17 2.Calculate each available driver’s ETA to the same pickup point based on current GPS location, driving speed, and number of existing passenger stops. 3.Compute the synchronization score as the absolute difference between arrival times: Synchronization_Score=|ET A passenger −ET A driver | 4.Assign the passenger to the driver with the lowest synchronization score. 5.If multiple drivers have similar scores, apply FCFS logic as a tiebreaker. This algorithm ensures efficient matching by minimizing the time gap between passen- ger and driver arrivals, reducing idle waiting time and improving overall system efficiency. 2.6Methodology The development of Wasselni transportation a

The feature vectors of all the plants the user has positively rated or interacted with can be averaged to create it. - Scoring and Ranking: A plant's score is determined by how closely it resembles the user profile. In order to do this, the cosine similarity between the user profile and each plant's feature vector must be determined. Next, the similarity scores of the plants are used to ra

ser profile and each plant's feature vector must be determined. Next, the similarity scores of the plants are used to rank them; higher scores suggest a better match to the user's tastes. - Top-N Recommendations: To suggest to the user, sort the top N plants based on their similarity ratings. By doing this, users may be guaranteed to see the most pertinent and customized material depending on their previous interactions and preferences. These actions will enable the Content-depending Filtering system to efficiently suggest plants to users depending on the specific characteristics of the plants and the user's preferences. There are two parties involved, drivers and passengers, and the app will facilitate their ride transactions so they split the travel costs. The app will benefit both drivers and passengers, as drivers can cover gas fees for their trip or even make a small profit while the passengers get to their destination faster
